text:
Maria Herrera: Quick question for the API folks — we need to align on 429 vs 503 semantics for per-route quotas and capacity failures. I'm updating the SDK behavior and want a single source of truth.
Kevin Zhou: Short answer: 429 = client hit a rate/quota boundary; 503 = service-side capacity problem or degraded infra. We shouldn't leak quota semantics as 503.
AJ Patel: To be explicit, when a per-route quota is exceeded we always return 429 plus rate-limit headers (not 503). For Dedicated capacity exhaustion (fallback) we may return 503 or 502 depending on failure mode.
Sophia Li: Agreed. Also we need to decide which headers go on the 429. Current shortlist: `Retry-After`, `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset`. Do we want any bucket id?
Kevin Zhou: We added `X-RW-RateLimit-Bucket` in the draft to disambiguate shared buckets (e.g., per-customer, per-route). That helps clients choose per-bucket backoff.
Maria Herrera: That's useful. Is the header value opaque or numeric? I prefer opaque token to avoid clients making assumptions about numeric semantics.
AJ Patel: Opaque token is fine. We'll keep numeric semantics in `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (unix epoch seconds).
Sophia Li: One more nuance: bursts. We allow brief spikes above steady rate using a token-bucket. If spike rejected, do we return a different code or include `X-RateLimit-Burst`?
Kevin Zhou: No new status code. Use 429. We can add `X-RW-Burst-Allowed` and `X-RW-Burst-Remaining` if you want clients to be more graceful. But keep header surface minimal for public API. Maybe only include `X-RW-Burst-Remaining` when burst is in play.
Maria Herrera: Sounds good. For backward compatibility: older SDKs expect `Retry-After` in seconds. Should we support both `Retry-After` (seconds) and `Retry-After-ISO`?
AJ Patel: Keep only `Retry-After` (seconds) for now. Simpler and widely supported. If we want ISO later we can add optional header but not required.
Sophia Li: About per-route vs global limits: when both apply, which header values do we expose? Aggregate or most-specific?
Kevin Zhou: Expose the most conservative (smallest remaining) plus a `X-RW-RateLimit-Scope: route|account|global` to indicate which limit fired. That helps clients decide fallback strategies.
Maria Herrera: Great. Can we put a short example in the API spec so SDK authors can implement backoff?
Kevin Zhou: Example 429 response in the spec:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Retry-After: 30
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1765432160
X-RW-RateLimit-Bucket: r_2a9f
X-RW-RateLimit-Scope: route
```

AJ Patel: Perfect. Also note we should include a short JSON body with machine-readable code and a human message, e.g. `{ "error": { "type": "rate_limit", "message": "Rate limit exceeded for /v1/generate" } }`.
Sophia Li: Ops question: how do we handle retries inside Redwood routing (automatic client retries)? We don't want DMA storms.
Kevin Zhou: We won't auto-retry for 429. For transient 503 we have a small automatic retry with jitter in the runtime for hosted customers, but not for Dedicated customer requests unless configured.
Maria Herrera: Last bit: logging for audits — please add `rate_limit_bucket` and `scope` to request logs so we can debug customer issues.
ops-bot: noted: created ticket INF-1207 to add headers to spec and log fields. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1207 :white_check_mark:
Maria Herrera: Thanks everyone — I'll update the SDK PR to rely on 429 semantics and those headers. Ping me if any objections. :thumbsup:
